component.name: Apache Helix
component.description: Generic cluster-management framework for partitioned, replicated, distributed resources: it assigns resource partitions to nodes, drives state transitions against a declarative state model, and reacts to node join/leave/failure. Helix is a coordination layer embedded by an operator's application; the ZooKeeper metadata store is the control-plane source of truth. It is not a standalone secure-by-default service.

externalReferences.comment: Source threat model (v1, authored by the ASF Security Team and ratified by the Helix PMC); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Helix cluster-management deployment
blueprints.description: Deployment described by the threat model: an operator stands up a ZooKeeper ensemble, runs a Controller, embeds the Participant in application nodes hosting resources, and optionally runs helix-rest for cluster administration. Untrusted actors appear at the helix-rest HTTP surface and wherever the ZooKeeper ensemble is reachable.

assets.name: helix-rest admin service
assets.description: Network-facing HTTP API to create/modify clusters, resources, instances, and configs. Shipped as a skeleton: the operator implements the authentication mechanism and the default is no auth. The primary network trust boundary.

assets.name: Cluster-management core (Controller / Participant / Spectator)
assets.description: helix-core roles that compute and apply state transitions via the metadata store. They run independent of user data and are trusted in-domain components.

assets.name: ZooKeeper metadata store
assets.description: The ZooKeeper-backed control plane Helix reads and writes (ideal state, external view, configs, messages). Whoever can write these znodes controls the cluster. ZooKeeper runs as a separate service; Helix sets no ACLs on the znodes it creates.

assets.name: Gateway / Agent integration surfaces
assets.description: helix-gateway and helix-agent are pluggable frameworks; the user supplies the implementation and its trust and network controls.

assets.name: Managed resources (operator's application)
assets.description: The databases/services/partitions hosted by Participants. Their security is the operator's application, not Helix; Helix coordinates placement and does not handle the resource payloads.

zones.name: Network clients
zones.description: Remote callers of helix-rest and any actor able to reach the ZooKeeper ensemble; untrusted-capable.

zones.name: Helix components
zones.description: Controller, Participant, Spectator, helix-rest, and gateway/agent surfaces; in-domain components are trusted and run independent of user data.

zones.name: ZooKeeper metadata store
zones.description: The real control plane, run as a separate service whose security (authN/authZ, ACLs, transport) is not Helix's responsibility.

zones.name: Operator and embedding application
zones.description: The operator and the application embedding the Participant/Spectator are trusted; they already control the cluster and what it hosts.

boundaries.name: Any actor to the ZooKeeper metadata store
Controller / Participant / Spectator coordination via the store

assumptions.description: Environment: a JVM; a reachable ZooKeeper ensemble (the control plane); the helix-rest listen interface; network reachability between Controller, Participants, and the ensemble; the system trust store if TLS is used.
Cluster/resource/instance configuration and state-model definitions are operator-supplied trusted control input.
ZooKeeper znode data is trusted-by-reliance: ZooKeeper access is gated by the ZooKeeper client's own authorization mechanism, and Helix sets no ACLs on the znodes it creates.
Out of scope: recipes, website, tests, and build files (not the shipped runtime); ZooKeeper's own security; the security of the resources Helix manages; build/release/supply-chain hygiene.

threats.name: Bypass of an operator-implemented helix-rest authentication layer
threats.description: For a deployment that has implemented authentication on helix-rest, an unauthenticated client mutating cluster state despite the operator's auth layer violates the access-control property; the model rates this critical. (An out-of-the-box unauthenticated deployment is the documented default, not a defect.)

threats.name: Unauthenticated cluster administration on a default helix-rest deployment
threats.description: helix-rest ships as a skeleton without built-in authentication; the default is no auth, so on an unprotected deployment an unauthenticated caller can administer a cluster (create clusters, add/drop resources, change configs, enable/disable instances). This posture is by design; implementing auth and restricting exposure is the operator's responsibility.

threats.name: Control-plane takeover via writable ZooKeeper ensemble
threats.description: An actor who can write the cluster's znodes can redirect partitions, disable nodes, or rewrite the state model, bypassing helix-rest entirely. An open or unauthenticated ZooKeeper ensemble reachable from an untrusted network means full control-plane takeover. ZooKeeper is a separate service the operator secures; Helix sets no ACLs on the znodes it creates and has no defense if ZooKeeper is open.

threats.name: Crash or corruption from malformed znode data
threats.description: A conditional surface: an actor who can inject malformed or forged znode data that a Controller, Participant, or Spectator parses. Parsing store contents should fail safe rather than crash or corrupt; a crash on malformed znode data in in-scope code is a valid finding.

threats.name: Network man-in-the-middle between components or on the REST channel
threats.description: A network MITM between Helix components (Controller, Participants, ensemble) or on the helix-rest channel is an in-scope adversary. The TLS posture of the helix-rest listen interface and the ZooKeeper client connection is an open question in the model; network isolation and TLS on sensitive channels are operator responsibilities.

threats.name: Hostile Controller or Participant inside the trust domain
threats.description: Helix provides no guarantee against a hostile Controller or Participant already inside the trust domain: they hold ZooKeeper write access by design. The operator and the embedding application are out-of-scope adversaries.

threats.name: Treating Helix as a security boundary for the resources it manages
threats.description: Helix is not a sandbox or isolation boundary for the databases, services, and partitions hosted by Participants; it places and transitions them, but their security (their own authentication and encryption) is the operator's application. Helix also adds no first-party authorization model or per-tenant RBAC; authorization is operator-implemented helix-rest auth plus ZooKeeper ACLs.

threats.name: Insecure operator-supplied gateway or agent implementations
threats.description: helix-gateway and helix-agent are pluggable frameworks: the user supplies the implementation, so its trust and network controls are the operator's responsibility. Findings against the deprecated Helix UI are likewise not actionable.

trustBoundaries.name: helix-rest trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: A network client issues cluster-admin operations. helix-rest ships as a skeleton with no default auth; the operator implements authentication. This is the high-value boundary.

trustBoundaries.name: ZooKeeper metadata-store trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The real control plane: an actor who can write the cluster's znodes controls the cluster, bypassing helix-rest entirely. Access is gated only by the ZooKeeper client's own authorization; Helix sets no ACLs on the znodes it creates.

trustBoundaries.name: Component coordination trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Controller, Participant, and Spectator coordinate by reading/writing znodes and trust the store's contents; malformed or forged znode data is a conditional surface.

trustBoundaries.name: Embedding trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The operator/application to embedded Participant/Spectator interface is in-process and trusted; the application already controls what it hosts.

controls.name: Implement helix-rest authentication and restrict exposure
controls.description: helix-rest ships as a skeleton with no default auth: the operator implements the authentication mechanism, must not expose the admin API to an untrusted network, and restricts who can mutate clusters.

controls.name: Secure the ZooKeeper ensemble
controls.description: ZooKeeper runs as a separate service that Helix does not manage; the operator handles its authorization (via the ZooKeeper client), authentication, and network isolation. Helix sets no ACLs on the znodes it creates, so any znode-level access control is the operator's.

controls.name: Fail-safe parsing of metadata-store contents
controls.description: Parsing store contents should fail safe rather than crash or corrupt; robustness to malformed znode data is a security property the project provides.

controls.name: Network-isolate components and use TLS on sensitive channels
controls.description: Network-isolate the Controller, Participants, and the ZooKeeper ensemble, and use TLS on sensitive channels. (The TLS default for the helix-rest listen interface and the ZooKeeper client connection is an open question in the model.)

controls.name: Secure the managed resources themselves
controls.description: The resources Helix manages need their own authentication and encryption; Helix is not a security boundary for them.

controls.name: Supply and secure gateway/agent implementations
controls.description: helix-gateway and helix-agent are pluggable frameworks; the operator provides the implementation together with its trust and network controls.
